question: Why does a match against a slightly better opponent feel more absorbing than an easy win?
answer: Because absorption needs a challenge right at the edge of skill. Csikszentmihalyi found that people report flow, the state of total focus in which time seems to vanish, when demands and ability are both high and matched. Too easy breeds boredom; too hard breeds anxiety. The best game is one that could be lost.
move: Seek tasks just beyond your ease, where losing is possible.
ask: What could I make slightly harder this week, so that I stop being bored by it?
reference: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience, Harper & Row, 1990
